activity.notes: Before Liu Bei's death in 223, he entrusted the young Liu Shan to Zhuge Liang. Zhuge then exercised the leading regency and handled state affairs until his death in 234. ATLAS records this de facto regency separately from the overlapping formal chancellorship.

sources.title: Zhuge Liang — ChinaKnowledge.de
sources.citation_text: ChinaKnowledge records Zhuge Liang as Liu Bei's senior military-political adviser, appointed Counsellor-in-chief in 221 and effectively regent under Liu Shan after Liu Bei's death.

sources.title: Zhuge Liang — Chinese Text Project
sources.citation_text: The Chinese Text Project account identifies Zhuge Liang as Imperial Chancellor from Shu Han's founding in 221 and regent from 223 until his death in 234.
